transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Apex - Head of ML), Ravi Patel (CTO), Jon Torres (Eng Manager)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes. quick intros, I'm Maya, AE, and Ethan is our SE who will run the demo.
[00:06] Ethan: hi all, excited to show how the hosted API works for chat and text generation, i'll start with the high-level then jump into a live console + streaming demo.
[00:15] Laura: great, we're mainly interested in low-latency personalization for search assistants and chat for our retail storefronts, also curious about cost tradeoffs.
[00:22] Ravi: and security — SOC2, encryption, VPC options — we need to map that to procurement.
[00:28] Ethan: totally, we'll cover those. quick agenda: API basics, streaming, params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), retry/backoff semantics, then console and quickstart code snippets.

[02:05] Ethan: first slide — Hosted API is a simple REST/SDK surface for chat, text generation and embeddings. we have curated models and performance profiles, you'll pick a model id and call /v1/generate or /v1/chat.
[02:30] Jon: are there SDKs? we primarily use node services.
[02:32] Maya: yes — official SDKs for node/python/go, examples in quickstart repo, link sent in chat (https://app.redwood.ai/quickstart). sometimes the transcript bot eats slashes so sorry if link looks off.

[05:10] Ethan: live console — showing a streaming response. note: streaming chunks are newline-delimited events, we support both SSE and chunked HTTP streaming. here i fire a chat request with messages and stream=true.
[05:35] Ethan: [typing demo] you'll see partial tokens arrive — good for instant UI updates. also partial deltas for function calling.
[06:02] Laura: how do you handle retries when streams get interrupted? we have flaky mobile networks.
[06:10] Ethan: good question. short answer: client should resume at message-level; our SDK exposes an idempotency key and a resume token for streaming in many cases. we also do server-side best-effort to keep sessions consistent but network resumptions are client-managed.
[06:30] Ravi: so if a stream disconnects mid-response we retry with same idempotency key and server will either continue or return a deterministic fallback?
[06:40] Ethan: yes, we surface retry status codes. if the model run was interrupted, the platform will usually return a 202 with a partial result, otherwise a 5xx triggers our recommended exponential backoff with jitter. default client retries in SDK are configurable.

[09:00] Ethan: walking params: temperature (0-1), top_p, max_tokens. for deterministic responses set temp=0 and top_p around 0.8; for more creative outputs bump temp to 0.8+. also show n=1 vs n>1 for multiple completions.
[09:34] Jon: what's best practice for stop sequences and token limits for chat bubbles?
[09:40] Ethan: use stop sequences for structured outputs, and keep max_tokens aligned with your UI limits — we show token estimation in the console. also enable prefix/KV caching when you reuse context across calls to cut cost.

[12:20] Ethan: demo 2: show retries in the SDK — set retry.policy=exponential, initial_backoff=200ms, max_attempts=4. i trigger a simulated 502 and show how client backs off and replays.
[12:55] Laura: curious about rate limits and quota shaping — our peak is bursts of 500 QPS for short periods.
[13:05] Maya: for hosted API we have tiered rate limits and quota; you can request increased throughput. for steady predictable throughput Dedicated is recommended but Hosted can handle bursts via autoscaling and burst credits.
[13:25] Ravi: what's the SLO on p95 latency for a 1k token response?
[13:32] Ethan: p95 depends on model and seq length — our performance profiles show numbers per model. for example the 'rwd-small-1' model p95 for 1k tokens is ~450ms per chunk on GPU-backed inference in our EU region — rough numbers, i'll attach the perf sheet.

[16:00] Ethan: about cost — tokens billed per input+output; streaming doesn't change billing semantics but can reduce perceived latency. batching and KV caching reduce per-token compute. Redwood Optimize will recommend batching and quantization for recurring patterns.
[16:35] Laura: can we do user-personalized caching without leaking across users?
[16:40] Ethan: yes, KV cache is per-session and you can scope caches to user IDs or hashed keys. for strict isolation you can use Dedicated or Private with customer-managed VPC.

[19:10] Maya: security overview — SOC 2 Type II, data encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integrations, audit logs in the console. VPC/private deployment options exist for regulated data.
[19:35] Ravi: do you support SSO and SCIM for user provisioning?
[19:38] Ethan: yes — SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC roles in console. we'll send the compliance pack.

[22:00] Ethan: now quickstart code snippet (node): call client.chat.create with stream=true and event handlers for data/chunk/end/error. i'll paste link to repo in chat.
[22:25] Jon: if we switch models for cheaper cost how do you handle compatibility for function calling and tool invocation?
[22:32] Ethan: model variants are labeled for compatibility. the router can fallback to compatible variants; function calling schema is preserved. you should test outputs with evals to ensure no regressions — Optimize helps with that.

[25:50] Ethan: live streaming demo — i'm sending a prompt that asks the model to generate product copy, you'll see token deltas, partial lines. note latency between chunks ~40-80ms depending on model.
[26:18] Laura: looks good. can we stream embeddings or is streaming only for text gen?
[26:22] Ethan: embeddings are synchronous, not streamed. streaming is for generative endpoints.

[29:05] Jon: what about retries for idempotent vs non-idempotent requests?
[29:10] Ethan: we recommend idempotency keys for mutation-like outputs. for pure generation you can treat requests as idempotent if you provide the same seed and keys, otherwise expect nondeterminism. our SDK exposes a request_id header for tracing.

[32:00] Ravi: procurement will want to see data residency in EU for our EU users — is region pinning available on hosted?
[32:10] Maya: yes, region pinning is available, we have EU, NA, APAC regions, and you can set a region in the API or via project settings. Private deployments give you full on-prem control.

[34:45] Ethan: quick note on observability: Console has token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, and traces. you can set alerts on quality regressions tied to eval prompt sets.
[35:12] Laura: can Optimize recommend quantization profiles?
[35:15] Ethan: yes — Optimize will suggest model variants, quantization levels and batching configs based on your workload to hit target latency/cost.

[37:50] Ravi: any gotchas we should know when moving from our current provider?
[38:00] Ethan: migration steps: map model APIs, run a pilot, run A/B tests with rollout policies. our rollout features include canary and automatic fallback. also share sample prompts and we'll run a small benchmark.

[41:20] Maya: recap and next steps — we'll send pricing and security docs, Ethan will share quickstart code and perf sheet, and Laura you'll share traffic profile so we can size a pilot.
[41:40] Laura: sounds good, aiming for pilot signoff in two weeks.
[41:50] Maya: thanks all, i'll follow up with calendar invites for a technical deep dive next week.
[42:05] Ravi: thanks, bye.
[42:10] Ethan: bye everyone.
